title: The Game Industry of Poland
publisher: Polish Agency for Enterprise Development (PARP) / Game Industry Conference / Indie Games Polska
years: 2016 and 2018 historical estimates; 2020 current workforce estimate
methodology: The report attributes the 2020 sector-size research to Game Industry Conference. It defines the counted population as game-production studios, external-development companies and global publishers. It excludes local-market distribution and non-production service providers; QA and localisation providers are discussed separately because their employment could not be consistently tracked. Detailed sample size and collection instrument were not stated in the inspected employment section.
assessment: Decisive primary source for the missing 2020 workforce point (9,710). Its backward-looking 2016 and 2018 counts are source-native restatements but must remain a separate, explicitly under-estimated historical-vintage series until their original sources and methods are recovered.
access_status: full public PDF downloaded and text-extracted; exact excerpts preserved in raw/GIofP_2020_decisive_extract.txt
next_step: Locate the original pre-2020 GIC estimates, if archived, before treating 2016 or 2018 as comparable to the 2020+ tighter estimate.

title: The Game Industry of Poland - Report 2021
publisher: Polish Agency for Enterprise Development (PARP) / Game Industry Conference
methodology: The report describes 9,710 in the 2020 edition as the first tight estimate reflected in statistical sources. Its 2021 population covers game-production stakeholders, including development studios, external-development services and global publishers, while excluding service-only localisation and player support.
assessment: Primary continuity evidence: it confirms the provenance and tightened status of the 2020 point, while retaining the existing 2021 observation. It does not validate the earlier 2016/2018 restatements as a continuous series.
access_status: full public PDF previously retained in base packet; public GIC mirror inspected in this pass
next_step: Keep the 2020+ core workforce series as an estimated industry series, not a payroll census or FTE series.

title: Raporty
years: archive listing: 2020, 2021, 2023; page current at the research date
methodology: Publisher archive describes the 2020 report as the first Polish publication with basic industry data including employment. It lists no annual 2022 or 2024 Game Industry of Poland edition and states that the 2023 report does not repeat exactly the 2020-2021 research scope.
assessment: Useful publisher-maintained archive map. It supports the report-edition gap but is not itself a workforce observation source.
next_step: Treat 2020, 2021, 2023 and 2025 as discrete publication snapshots; do not interpolate 2022 or 2024.

title: The latest edition of the report on the Polish games industry: The Game Industry of Poland 2025
methodology: PARP identifies the 2025 report's partners as the Ministry of Development and Technology, Institute of Creative Industries and Game Industry Conference. The base packet's full 2025 PDF records 14,568 people with an October 2025 active-studio frame and notes improved studio-discovery methodology.
assessment: No later source-native Polish game-production employment reference year was located in this bounded forward sweep. The existing 2025 observation remains the latest verified point; release timing is not a new 2026 employment observation.
access_status: official public release inspected; underlying 2025 PDF already retained in base packet
next_step: Watch PARP/GIC and Indie Games Polska for the next report; verify its reference date, studio frame and any revised historical employment values before extending the core series.
